From: Jack Sullivan <jack@acme.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant activation: network diagram + preflight questions

Hi Grace / Lauren,

Thanks for taking this on — we're excited to get Acme AI spun up on Redwood Private. Attached is our initial network diagram (acme_network_diagram_v1.pdf). We have a few immediate preflight asks to make sure the first-week activation is smooth:

- Desired hosting model: single-tenant VPC with cross-account peering to Redwood-managed gateway (is that supported in your EU/US footprint?).
- Egress requirements: analytics exports to our S3 in us-west-2 (we may need NAT + static egress IPs).
- Port list: we'll need 443 outbound to your control plane, and ports 9200/9300 to our monitoring endpoint (or a push proxy).
- KMS: we use a customer-managed KMS key (AWS KMS) and need CMEK guidance and audit evidence.

Can you confirm who owns the routing (Redwood or Acme) and whether you can provide a preflight checklist we can use internally? Also happy to hop on a quick 30m tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jack Sullivan
Head of Infrastructure, Acme AI
jack@acme.ai

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant activation: network diagram + preflight questions

Jack — thanks for the diagram and clear asks. We're happy to lead the activation routing and provide the preflight checklist. Quick answers up front:

- Hosting model: single-tenant VPC (Redwood-managed peering) is supported in our US regions; we can discuss EU if you later need multi-region.
- Egress: static egress IPs are available as an add-on; we'll need the destination CIDR for the S3 endpoints.
- Ports: 443 outbound to control plane required; for monitoring, we typically recommend an agent that pushes over TLS (443) to avoid opening 9200/9300 inbound. If you must host a pull endpoint, we'll add it to the allowlist.
- KMS/CMEK: supported via cross-account grant; we will need the key ARN and an IAM principal for the workload.

I'm looping Ben for the runbook and Lauren for access/ownership handoff. Ben — can you attach the Private Preflight matrix (template) and highlight the fields Acme must fill? Lauren — can we pencil a 30m preflight tomorrow 11:00 PT?

Next steps I propose (high level):
1) Share completed preflight matrix (Acme)
2) Exchange KMS/key ARN and grant details
3) Confirm egress static IPs or alternative export plan
4) Schedule runbook walk and smoke test

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Adding the Private Preflight matrix (redwood_private_prereq_matrix.xlsx) — Ben's notes embedded:

- Ownership: Redwood will own the peering and routing config for the tenant VPC. Acme remains owner of their customer VPC and on-prem connectors.
- SLOs: we aim for control plane <150ms API p95 for activation flows; please flag any tighter requirements.
- VPN vs Peering: peering is preferred for performance; if Acme requires IPSec VPN for policy reasons, we can accommodate but it adds provisioning and rotation steps.
- Ports: prefer agent/push model to avoid inbound openings. If monitoring cannot push, we need a static inbound STUN port list — please indicate in the matrix.
- CIDR overlap: send a full CIDR list (primary + secondary) to avoid conflicts.
- KMS: we require a grant to redwood-inference@redwood.ai with key usage for encrypt/decrypt by service principal (we'll provide an AWS principal ARN).

Attachment: redwood_private_prereq_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 rows)

I'll copy select runbook snippets into the matrix for the smoke test: NAT verification, route table check, TLS cert verification, and a minimal inference request with sample token counts.

—Ben
